title: Three-Dimensional Echocardiographic Method for the Visualization and Assessment of Specific Parameters of the Pulmonary Veins
protocol: Ensure at least a 4-hour fasting status for the patient.
Administer a questionnaire about problems with swallowing and known upper gastrointestinal diseases.
Read and ensure written informed consent is signed by the patient.
Prepare an intravenous line before the examination.
Position the patient in a left lateral decubitus position.
Administer mild sedation using intravenous midazolam (2.5-5 mg).
Monitor ECG and oxygen saturation.
Insert the probe into the oesophagus at approximately 30-40 cm from the front teeth.
Visualize the LAA using 2D image acquisition at 20-45° in the upper or mid transoesophageal probe position.
Turn the probe slightly clockwise to change the crystal angulation to 60-80° to centralize the LAA on the image.
Click the full volume button for applying full volume 3D acquisition.
Adjust the image’s lateral and elevational width to display the LAA and the left upper PV.
Optimize the image quality by adjusting depth and gain, and applying harmonic imaging.
Record a one-beat (if feasible, multibeat) loop with 2 cardiac cycles.
Change the angulation to approximately 120° on the 2D image to centralize the LAA.
Turn the probe slightly counterclockwise and apply anteflexion to visualize the ostia of the left PVs.
Apply color Doppler-coded imaging to confirm that both the upper and lower PVs are visible.
Click the full volume button to initiate full volume 3D acquisition.
Adjust the image’s lateral and elevational width to display the left PVs.
Crop the image to the upper or lower PV ostium, respectively, to enhance visualization of the PV ostia.
If the dataset does not contain both the upper and lower PVs, change the patient position by further tilting to the lateral position, and repeat from step 2.1.8.
Acquire 3D full volume datasets from the left PVs: one-beat (if feasible, multibeat) loop with 2 cardiac cycles.
Confirm the visibility of PV ostia by cropping the image to the upper or lower PV ostium, respectively.
If the image is not suitable for visualizing the complete PV structure, repeat the procedure from step 2.1.10.
Change the lateral or elevational width of the 3D dataset if necessary.
Switch back to 2D mode and focus the image to the LAA at 45° upper (or mid) oesophageal probe position.
Turn the probe clockwise.
Move the probe head to anteflexion position.
Apply color Doppler-coded imaging.
Click the full volume button for full volume 3D acquisition.
Adjust the image’s lateral width.
Adjust the image’s elevational width.
Crop the image to display the upper PV ostium.
Crop the image to display the lower PV ostium.
Tilt the patient position to the right if necessary.
Change the lateral or elevational width of the 3D dataset as needed.
Activate the 3D analysis software on your scanner or workstation.
Select a frame in diastolic phase for the measurements.
Set the two perpendicular planes to the requested structure.
Adjust plane direction while the third plane represents the en face view of the examined structure.
On the left panel, select the measurement option.
The en face view is suitable for measurements.
